Anti-CD20 B-cell depleter. Approved oncology; widely used off-label in autoimmune. Does NOT deplete plasma cells (CD20−). Relapses common in 6–12 months as plasma cells replenish autoantibodies. Ritual evidence: B-cell depletion works in autoimmune, but CD20 is insufficient — need to reach plasma cell compartment (BCMA). Sets the stage for why CD19+BCMA dual targeting is needed.

CD19×CD3 bispecific. Approved in ALL. PoC in RA (Bucci Nature Medicine 2024): drug-free remission. Requires continuous IV infusion (hospital/pump). Misses bone marrow plasma cells (BCMA−). The proof-of-concept that off-the-shelf CD19×CD3 can reset autoimmunity — ACE adds BCMA arm + off-the-shelf SC format to make this mechanism practical.

BCMA×CD3 bispecific. Approved MM. PoC in SLE (Alexander NEJM 2024): clinical remission + autoantibody reduction. Clears bone marrow plasma cells. Misses circulating B cells (CD19+). Requires SC Q1W dosing for myeloma — patients need access to certified center. ACE combines CD19 (circulatory) + BCMA (marrow) + CD3 in one off-the-shelf product.

Mackensen/Müller group (NEJM 2024): CD19 CAR-T in 15 patients — complete remission, drug-free. But: requires lymphodepletion (Cy/Flu), hospital admission, 2–8 week manufacturing, ~$400K+. ACE is the off-the-shelf equivalent that makes this depth of B-cell depletion accessible without CAR-T infrastructure.
